sources.title: Interview note containing the multithreaded transfer coding prompt
Answer Batch 0018 mechanically extracted repository-source packet
Deterministic Java validation for the selected in-memory transfer contract
Source-first isolated review for the concurrent-transfer candidate

claims.text: The retained repository source explicitly asks for a transfer implementation under multithreading and does not specify account representation, failure semantics, lock primitive, persistence or database/distributed transaction behavior.

Single-JVM in-memory accounts, unique long ids, non-negative long balances, positive amounts, boolean insufficient-funds behavior, self-transfer no-op, duplicate-id rejection and overflow behavior are explicit candidate choices rather than source facts.

Holding both account locks across the balance check, both new-balance computations and both assignments implements an indivisible successful state transition for callers following the selected in-memory protocol.
Acquiring the two account locks by ascending unique account id prevents the opposite lock order of concurrent A-to-B and B-to-A transfers within this protocol.

The exact Java fixture passes fixed contract cases plus 160000 opposing-direction operations and 60000 deterministic random operations while confirming progress, conservation and non-negative balances.

findings: The candidate stays within the source-supported multithreaded-transfer goal and explicitly limits its execution model.
The double-lock critical section and ascending-id order are consistent with the implementation and stress tests.
Failure atomicity for insufficient funds and overflow is covered by executable checks.
No database/distributed or personal production claims are introduced.
Formal promotion remains blocked only by the required human-approval gate.
